s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, accompanied by systemic symptoms such as fever and arthralgia, and neurological complications
salient_findings: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Neurological complications are present
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history is negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis have been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Aqueous tap PCR results are positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
IgM CHIKV serologic test is positive

shortlist.why_kept: Positive aqueous tap PCR results and positive IgM CHIKV serologic test

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation

shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and neurological complications

raw.rationale: The patient's positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load, along with the clinical presentation of bilateral blurred vision, ocular irritation, and recent history of fever and arthralgia, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: Aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: No specific evidence of Toxoplasmosis was found in the vignette, such as characteristic retinochoroiditis.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the typical granulomatous uveitis and panuveitis seen in Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease.

rejected.label: Behcet's disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of oral or genital ulcers, which are common in Behcet's disease.

rejected.label: Sympathetic ophthalmia
rejected.why: The patient's ocular history is negative for trauma, which is a common precursor to sympathetic ophthalmia.

rejected.label: Phlyctenular keratoconjunctivitis
rejected.why: The clinical findings do not match the typical presentation of phlyctenular keratoconjunctivitis, which includes small, nodular lesions on the bulbar conjunctiva or cornea.

rejected.label: Zika virus infection
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of Zika virus infection provided in the vignette, such as positive PCR results for Zika virus.

rejected.label: Syphilis
rejected.why: Syphilis has been ruled out according to the vignette.
